gap: No result ChatGPT got pairs each NAS's price today with its single-thread score. On 2026-11-08 the UGREEN DXP4800 Plus costs $619.99 at UGREEN's store and scores 3,197 on PassMark single-thread. The QNAP TS-464 costs $599–$639 on Amazon and scores 1,492 (Celeron N5095). The Synology DS925+ costs $819.99 on Amazon and scores 1,136 (Ryzen V1500B). Single-thread speed is what a Minecraft Java server depends on.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited rival pages. racksandwatts.com/guides/best-nas-for-a-homelab-2026 lists the DXP2800, DS225+, DXP4800 Plus and DS925+ with CPU and RAM only. It has 'Check price on Amazon' links but prints no price, and it says nothing about Minecraft, single-thread speed or benchmarks. esp32.co.uk/best-4-bay-nas-for-docker-plex-and-family-storage lists the DS925+, TS-464, DXP4800 Plus and TerraMaster F4-425 Plus with CPU and RAM. It also prints no prices, and it has no Minecraft or benchmark data. The UGREEN product pages ChatGPT cited cover only UGREEN models. ChatGPT's own answer said in words that single-core speed matters, but no source it got gives a number or a price.
decides: This confirms the DXP4800 Plus as the 4-bay pick and settles it against ChatGPT's QNAP alternative. For $619.99 you get more than twice the TS-464's single-thread score (3,197 vs 1,492), which costs the same or more ($639 per ChatGPT's B&H card, $599–$639 on Amazon). The Synology DS925+ costs the most of the 4-bays ($819.99 on Amazon) and has the slowest single thread (1,136), so it loses for Minecraft despite the brand. On the budget side, the DXP2800 at $389.99 (N100, 1,879) beats the DS225+ at $364.29 (J4125, 1,151, 2 GB RAM). A separate cost warning: TerraMaster's own 16 GB DDR5 upgrade stick is listed at $469.99, more than a whole DXP2800. A box that ships with enough RAM beats planning to upgrade later.
